sections.title: Goal and intuition
sections.learning_objective: Explain relational tables, primary keys and foreign keys.
sections.markdown: A relational table records one kind of thing in rows; named columns describe it. A primary key identifies a row uniquely and cannot be NULL. A foreign key constrains references to another table: it is not automatically unique. A nullable foreign key may be NULL; NOT NULL is a separate requirement. Think of each library member having one member number, while many loan rows can refer to that number.
key_points: A foreign key does not imply a one-to-one relationship.

sections.title: A worked example and why it works
sections.learning_objective: Explain relational tables, primary keys and foreign keys.
sections.markdown: Suppose members has primary key id with rows 2 and 8. Loans has its own primary key id and a nullable member_id referencing members(id). Two loans may both refer to member 2. A loan with member_id 99 is invalid because no member 99 exists. A NULL member_id is allowed unless NOT NULL is added. To inspect existing identifiers, `SELECT id FROM members ORDER BY id` returns 2 then 8. ORDER BY is needed when order matters; storage order is not a result guarantee.

examples.explanation: Read supplied member identifiers in an explicit order.

sections.title: Guided practice, independent practice and revision
sections.learning_objective: Explain relational tables, primary keys and foreign keys.
sections.markdown:
Guided: distinguish members.id, which identifies a member, from loans.member_id, which refers to one. To find loans without an assigned member use `WHERE member_id IS NULL`; `= NULL` is not that test. Independent: can members with IDs 2 and 8 share the same display name?

<details><summary>Reasoning</summary>Yes, if only id is the primary key and name has no uniqueness constraint. A display name is not necessarily an identifier. Conversely, inserting id 2 twice violates the primary key.</details>

Revision: state what each row represents, find its primary key, describe each reference, consider nullable fields, and state result ordering. Forge Run/Submit use disposable PGlite databases. Learner SQL never runs against Forge history. The coding items inspect supplied schemas; they do not claim to assess unrestricted database administration or live application migrations.
